registers.label: Spare
lines: The stone is rolled across the tomb; the seal is set.
We wait for the Lord in the silence.
If mortals die, will they live again?
Into your hand we commit our spirits.
The whole earth keeps a sabbath of grief.
We wait for the Lord in the silence.
Come, let us keep watch until the morning.
We wait for the Lord in the silence. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: A stone is rolled across the mouth of the grave, the soldiers take their post, the seal is pressed into the clay, and everything goes still.
We wait for the Lord in the silence.
This is the day with no liturgy, the long sabbath of God, the in-between hours when the Lord of life lies among the dead.
We wait for the Lord in the silence.
Job's old question hangs in the air: if a mortal dies, will they live again? and the tomb gives back no answer yet.
We wait for the Lord in the silence.
Into your hand we commit our spirits; you are our rock and our refuge; even here you have not let us go.
We wait for the Lord in the silence.
So keep watch through the dark with us; do not be afraid of the quiet. Come, let us wait and worship.
We wait for the Lord in the silence. Amen.

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: The stone is sealed; the soldiers keep their watch.
We wait for the Lord in the silence.
If mortals die, will they live? Into your hand we commit all.
We wait for the Lord in the silence.
The earth keeps a long sabbath of grief.
We wait for the Lord in the silence.
Come, let us keep watch until the morning.
We wait for the Lord in the silence. Amen.
